description: The S_4 bridge is nearly vacuous: the S_4-invariant ternary quartics form a pencil, so infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic genus-3 curves admit S_4. Bean qou-8p1a (parent qou-8pl1).

computation.arithmetic: exact Fraction / Z / Q(sqrt d); no floating point

group.construction: G = V_4 : S_3 < GL_3(Z), even sign changes and coordinate permutations
group.pins_S4_because: profile {1:1,2:9,3:8,4:6} is unique to S_4 among the fifteen groups of order 24; SL(2,3) shares the 3- and 4-counts but has one involution and eight elements of order 6

pencil.parameter_name_note: this module calls the pencil parameter L (Python reserves 'lambda'); the eightfold-way chapter calls it t, deliberately not lambda, which denotes a partition there

data.verdict: Infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic genus-3 curves admit a faithful S_4 action, so 'S_4 survives the pinch' has essentially no selecting power for the Klein quartic.
data.moduli_argument: Distinct L give non-proportional defining forms. For fixed mu, {L : C_L iso C_mu} is finite because Aut(C_mu) is finite (genus >= 2) and N_{PGL_3}(S_4) is finite (its centralizer is trivial by the scalar commutant in C4, so it embeds in Aut(S_4)). Finite fibres over a P^1 meet infinitely many isomorphism classes. NOTE: only finiteness of Aut is used -- the sharp Hurwitz bound is deliberately avoided, an earlier step of this arc having been withdrawn for misusing it.

consequence_for_siblings.qou-8p1b: insufficient as written -- separating Klein from Fermat does not single out Klein from an infinite family; re-scope to an invariant the pinch itself determines
consequence_for_siblings.qou-8p1c: not the bottleneck -- period matrices of two hand-picked curves cannot close an argument whose datum is this weak

not_verified_here: the value of L at which the Klein quartic sits in this pencil (needs arithmetic over Q(sqrt(-7)))
hyperelliptic genus-3 curves admitting S_4, which lie outside the pencil and only enlarge the competitor set
data.scope: scope-(a). Refutes the S_4 bridge AS AN ARGUMENT for the Bring->Klein degeneration. Does NOT refute the degeneration itself, which remains open.
